Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent

Class EloquentBuilder<T extends Model>

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.EloquentBuilder<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the model class
public final class EloquentBuilder<T extends Model> extends Object
A query on one model's table that returns models: Laravel's Eloquent builder over the core query builder.

Clause methods forward to the wrapped Builder and return this builder, so the SQL is the query builder's. Read methods turn rows into models of T that exist, are clean and have had their retrieved() hook run. Methods change this builder, as Laravel's do; start a new one from ModelQuery.query() for each query. Not safe to share across threads.

Relations named with with(String...) are eager loaded after each read that returns models: get(), first() and the finds built on them, each chunk, each page and each buffer of lazy(int). cursor() refuses them.

      public Optional<T> find(Object id)
      Finds a model by its primary key.

      Returns:
      the model, or empty
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if id is a Collection

      Streams the models through one open QueryCursor; close it, best with try-with-resources. stream() on it releases the connection only when the stream is closed.

      Eager loads are refused: loading them per row would run one query per model, and Laravel ignores them here. lazy(int) reads in pages and eager loads each page.

      The casts and the row hook are read once, when the cursor opens; a change to this builder afterwards does not reach rows already streaming.

      The cursor holds its session until it is closed, so a long loop over it leaves a PostgreSQL connection idle in transaction. Writing through the same database inside the loop needs a second connection, and a pool of one deadlocks. Use lazy(int) for a slow loop or one that writes.

      Returns:
      the open cursor, never null
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if eager loads are set

    • withCasts

      public final EloquentBuilder<T> withCasts(Map<String,?> casts)
      Casts columns of every model this builder reads, on top of the model's own casts, as ModelCasts.mergeCasts(Map) does for one model. The casts are in place before retrieved() runs. Models of eager loaded relations are not affected.

      Calls merge: a later call adds to the earlier ones and wins for a key in both, so the casts withExists registers survive. The values are resolved now, so a bad cast fails here; the map is not kept.

      Parameters:
      casts - the casts by column, each a Cast or a cast string, never null; an empty map changes nothing
      Returns:
      this builder
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if casts or a key in it is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if a value is null or neither a cast nor a string
      InvalidCastException - if a cast string cannot be resolved

    • with

      public final EloquentBuilder<T> with(String... relations)
      Eager loads relations with the models this builder reads.

      A dot path such as "posts.comments" loads each level. "posts:id,title" selects only those columns of the relation; the key the relation matches on is added when left out. Naming a path twice runs both constraints, the earlier first. Names are checked when the models are loaded, not here.

      Parameters:
      relations - the relation paths, none null
      Returns:
      this builder
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if a path is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if a name:columns path lists an empty column

    • with

      public final EloquentBuilder<T> with(String relation, Consumer<EloquentBuilder<?>> constraint)
      Eager loads one relation, letting a callback constrain its query.

      The callback runs once per key chunk of the eager query, plus once on a probe query that is never run. A limit or offset in it is refused when the relation loads. The relation keys are filtered first, so an orWhere in the callback must be grouped, as in Laravel.

      Parameters:
      relation - the relation path, never null; a :columns part is not parsed
      constraint - the constraint on the relation's query, never null
      Returns:
      this builder
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null

    • upsert

      public final int upsert(List<? extends Map<String,?>> rows, List<String> uniqueBy)
      Inserts the rows, and where a row conflicts on the unique columns, sets every column of the first row from the row that was refused, plus updated_at.

      Like Laravel, it goes straight to the database: no model events run and no casts apply. Rows without the key of a model that generates unique ids get one. A model that keeps timestamps gets created_at and updated_at on every row, one moment for all of them, unless the row names the column; updated_at joins the columns that are updated, created_at does not.

      Parameters:
      rows - the rows, never null, all with the same columns
      uniqueBy - the columns of the unique index that decides a conflict, never null or empty
      Returns:
      the number of rows written, as the database reports it; 0 for no rows
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument or a row is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if uniqueBy is empty or the rows are not alike
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the database cannot upsert, as SQLite before 3.24
      QueryException - if the database refuses the statement

    • upsert

      public final int upsert(List<? extends Map<String,?>> rows, List<String> uniqueBy, List<String> update)
      Inserts the rows, and where a row conflicts on the unique columns, sets the named columns from the row that was refused, plus updated_at when the model keeps timestamps; see EloquentCreators.upsert(List, List).
      Parameters:
      rows - the rows, never null, all with the same columns
      uniqueBy - the columns of the unique index that decides a conflict, never null or empty
      update - the columns to take from the refused row; null for every column of the first row as given; an empty list leaves a conflicting row as it is, with no updated_at either
      Returns:
      the number of rows written, as the database reports it; 0 for no rows
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if rows, uniqueBy or a row is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if uniqueBy is empty or the rows are not alike
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the database cannot upsert, as SQLite before 3.24
      QueryException - if the database refuses the statement

    • insertOrIgnore

      public final int insertOrIgnore(List<? extends Map<String,?>> rows)
      Inserts the rows in one statement, skipping each that would break a unique or primary key constraint. No model events run. Rows without the key of a model that generates unique ids get one, and a model that keeps timestamps gets them, one moment for all rows, unless a row names the column.
      Parameters:
      rows - the rows, never null, all with the same columns
      Returns:
      the number of rows inserted, as the database reports it; 0 for no rows
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if rows or a row is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the rows are not alike
      QueryException - if the database refuses the insert

    • fillAndInsert

      public final boolean fillAndInsert(List<? extends Map<String,?>> rows)
      Fills a model from each row, then inserts the rows in one statement: Laravel's fillAndInsert. The fill is unguarded, so fillable is not checked: never pass request data here unchecked. Casts apply, unique ids are generated and timestamps are set, one moment for all rows, but a given created_at or updated_at is kept. beforeWrite() runs on each row's model, and no model event fires. It is one statement, so the database's binding limit applies (999 on SQLite before 3.32).
      Parameters:
      rows - the rows, never null, all with the same columns
      Returns:
      true when the insert ran, also for no rows, which run no query
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if rows or a row is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the filled rows are not alike
      QueryException - if the database refuses the insert

    • fillAndInsertOrIgnore

      public final int fillAndInsertOrIgnore(List<? extends Map<String,?>> rows)
      Fills a model from each row, then inserts the rows in one statement, skipping each that would break a unique or primary key constraint: Laravel's fillAndInsertOrIgnore. The fill is unguarded, so fillable is not checked: never pass request data here unchecked. Casts apply, unique ids are generated and timestamps are set, but a given created_at or updated_at is kept. beforeWrite() runs on each row's model, and no model event fires. It is one statement, so the database's binding limit applies (999 on SQLite before 3.32).
      Parameters:
      rows - the rows, never null, all with the same columns
      Returns:
      the number of rows inserted, as the database reports it; 0 for no rows, which run no query
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if rows or a row is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the filled rows are not alike
      QueryException - if the database refuses the insert

    • fillAndInsertGetId

      public final Object fillAndInsertGetId(Map<String,?> row)
      Fills a model from one row, inserts it and returns its key: Laravel's fillAndInsertGetId. A model with an incrementing key returns the key the database made; any other returns the key value in the filled row, a generated unique id included. The fill is unguarded, so fillable is not checked: never pass request data here unchecked. Casts apply, unique ids are generated and timestamps are set, but a given created_at or updated_at is kept. beforeWrite() runs on the model, and no model event fires.
      Parameters:
      row - the columns and values, never null
      Returns:
      the key, or null when a model without an incrementing key has none in the row
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if row is null
      QueryException - if the database refuses the insert
